paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: everything good you have was handed to you, so there's nothing to strut about. Paul asks, "What do you have that you did not receive?" (1 Corinthians 4:7). The Corinthians were picking favorite teachers like it was a trophy shelf, but Paul says to see us as "servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God" (1 Corinthians 4:1). And the one thing a steward must be is faithful, not famous (1 Corinthians 4:2).

Now, who gets to grade the work? Paul says it's not the crowd, and it's not even his own gut. "My conscience is clear, but that does not vindicate me. It is the Lord who judges me" (1 Corinthians 4:4). Baker, me announcing "these cookies are DONE" has never once made them done, so I'm happy to let the One who sees everything call it. That means we can stop campaigning for applause and "judge nothing before the appointed time" (1 Corinthians 4:5), because "each will receive his praise from God."

Paul isn't scolding from a throne, either. He writes as a father, "not to shame you, but to warn you as my beloved children" (1 Corinthians 4:14). He tells them "the kingdom of God is not a matter of talk but of power" (1 Corinthians 4:20), and he'd much rather come "in love and with a gentle spirit" (1 Corinthians 4:21). So, friend, here's your takeaway: serve faithfully, stay humble about what you've been given, and let the Lord do the judging. That's one lesson in the Divisions in the Church group, and with this passage, the group is done.
